claims.text: Atomic-scale chemical disorder predominantly governs superconducting transition temperature in high-entropy alloys.
Atomic-scale chemical disorder predominantly governs the upper critical field in high-entropy alloys.
Mixing entropy is a quantitative measure of atomic-scale chemical disorder.
Chemical disorder perturbs electron-phonon coupling.
Chemical disorder alters the local electronic density of states.
The mixing entropy can be systematically varied by changing the proportions and number of principal elements.
The proposed comparison will vary mixing entropy while maintaining constant electron count and valence states.
High configurational entropy produces altered local atomic configurations and associated lattice distortions.
Entropy-induced local configurations and lattice distortions affect phonon modes.
Entropy-induced local configurations and lattice distortions affect the density of states at the Fermi level.
Increased chemical disorder introduces additional scattering centers.
Disorder-related scattering perturbs phonon-mediated Cooper pairing.
Disorder reduces the effective electron-phonon coupling strength.
High mixing entropy can lower the density of states at the Fermi level.
At similar electron counts, alloys with higher mixing entropy will have lower transition temperatures than lower-entropy baselines.
At similar electron counts, alloys with higher mixing entropy will exhibit a shifted upper critical field.
Increasing configurational disorder will produce a monotonic or statistically significant reduction in superconducting parameters.
Reducing the number of principal elements or choosing chemically similar elements necessarily yields a more ordered lattice.
The disorder mechanism should dominate when electron-count variation, magnetic impurities, and strong spin-orbit effects are negligible and pairing is conventional and phonon mediated.
Electron-count changes and local structural effects can confound the relationship between mixing entropy and superconductivity.

contradictions.description: The intervention and baseline vary mixing entropy by changing element number, identity, or proportions, whereas the falsification design requires samples to have identical overall composition except for configurational disorder. Composition-derived mixing entropy cannot be changed by those proposed routes while overall composition remains identical; an ordering or annealing-based route would be needed instead.
